protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; one owner-recording entry for the DR-011 parent under adopted D-054 / D-057, v3 plus three riders
summary: Subject and prompt held at their dispatched digests, both read-only. This is the last of the eleven inherited rows to be owner-recorded, and the check that mattered most to me was whether the recording preserves the bound that v3 had to be rejected once to acquire. It does: clause 2 carries 'This parent adds no independent semantic permission' into the recording itself, and the entry grants no surface of its own. All three riders are carried three times each — header, disposition pin, and the operative clause — and the advisory classification declares all three operative under D-057 clause 3. I walked that clause's pin list element by element and all thirteen are present, including the D-054 path and the strengthened MF-6 reversal limb that earlier entries in this family had to be told to add. Six digests and four commits verify, the Route A remainder is an exact three-item match, and the owner role matches file 08 character for character.
whatIVerified: Prompt digest at start and end: e9031acdfb5624a5b3603812c37fbd2c9bd96e495cc95ddc3138ba8a02257c6e, equal to the dispatch-supplied value. Subject at 1ad58b169d4328919a190bf8576f6b18cf4db296763b0c077f01d43980f6d41d, equal to both. Three measurements each at start and again at end; both -r--r--r-- at both ends.

The recording does not re-widen what v3 narrowed, which is the check I prioritised because v2 of that disposition was rejected precisely for an unbounded grant. v3's repair states that residual-dependent recipes, schemas, identities, exits, custody, proof, checker standing and product boundaries gain no design permission from the parent; D-083 clause 2 carries the operative sentence — 'This parent adds no independent semantic permission' — and the entry itself contains no whatMayBeDesigned-style grant. So the bound survives the step from disposition to owner recording rather than being dropped at the point where it would matter most.

The attack 'drops a rider' fails. Each of RB-DR011-V3-A1, RB-DR011-V3-A2 and RB-DR011-V3-A3 appears three times: in the header's 'Does owner-record … as v3 plus riders' line, in the disposition pin's '**plus riders**' clause with a one-line description each, and in clause 1's operative recording. All three are also defined in adopted D-082, so the entry inherits them rather than re-deriving them.

The rider descriptions are faithful and, on the one that could have been inverted, correctly directed. A1 is 'propertyPins restored', A2 is 'R06/R07 stay NARROWED', and A3 is 'R16 cites DR-010 not D-010' — the same direction D-082 records, 'namedD055Consequences.R16 cites **DR-010**, not D-010'. I checked that orientation specifically because D-010 and DR-010 both exist in the corpus and denote unrelated things, and an inverted correction would have looked identical at a glance.

The advisory classification satisfies D-057 clause 3: 'all three advisories are **operative** riders (same form as D-039 / D-076). They do not close residuals.' That is classify-and-carry rather than classify-away, and the D-039 / D-076 precedent is the right one — both are adopted rider-carrying instruments.

I ran D-057 clause 3's pin list element by element and all thirteen are present: the dependency declaration with its revocation sentence naming D-054, D-057 and D-055; the D-054 path with sha256 and commit; the D-057 commit; the Route B selection D-055 commit; the coordinator recording D-082 commit; the disposition path with sha256; the operative-riders marker on that pin; both verdict paths with sha256 and recited verdicts; the owner role; the preview scope; the advisory classification; the attributed Route A remainder; and the MF-6 reversal limb in its strengthened form, 'plus reconciliation of any later MF-6 note under its own reviewed act'.

The attack 'missing D-054 path or MF-6 reversal' therefore fails on both counts. These are the two elements D-078 turn 1 dropped and had to restore at turn 2; this entry carries both from the outset, along with the dependency-direction sentence 'Revoking or overturning D-054, D-057, or D-055 requires superseding this owner record' in the reversibility clause.

All six cited digests match live bytes: COORD 2f3947b8…, file 08 1360a4f8…, the D-054 amendment c274d140…, the v3 disposition f1c7f6b7…, my verdict 46ec1329…, and the Codex verdict bd6a8c2f… (hashed, not opened). My verdict recital is exact — that file records ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES with 0 blockers and one advisory under the id RBDR011V3-C2-A1, precisely as cited.

All four cited commits resolve at full hash with subjects matching their claimed roles: 29670ed D-054, 33597e8 D-057, 5acba0fe 'D-055: select Route B for DR-011 parent (preview scope)', and e6460ea3 'D-082: record DR-011 preview disposition v3 plus riders'. All four decisions are present in COORD and ADOPTED, and D-083 is not yet present so adoption creates no collision.

The Route A remainder is complete, tested by string equality against the v3 disposition's whatRemainsOwedOnRouteA: three items each, exact match, same order — individual CLOSED or LAWFULLY-DISPOSED evidence for every residual; R10 after all surface adjudications and V10 resolution; parent SATISFIED only after residuals close or are lawfully disposed.

The owner role is an exact string match: file 08's DR-011 owner cell reads 'V1 coordinator and each surface owner' and the entry pins the identical string. DR-011's status cell still leads HARD-BLOCKED, matching clause 3.

The attacks 'silent SATISFIED' and 'closes any residual' fail: the header refuses both, clause 3 states 'Does not mark DR-011 SATISFIED. Does not close any residual', clause 2 adds 'Residuals stay not CLOSED', and the readiness effect repeats 'Residuals stay not CLOSED. Zero SATISFIED. Conditions 2–5 unchanged.'

The attack 'bundles another row' fails, and the unnamed form is correct here rather than a weakening. The header and clause 5 both state 'Does not owner-record any other row' without naming siblings, which the earlier entries in this family did — but there are no un-recorded siblings left. All nine of DR-002 through DR-010 already carry preview-scope owner-recording notes in file 08, DR-001 is SATISFIED, and DR-011 carries none. This is the last row, so there is nothing to enumerate.

The attacks 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' and 'file 08 edited' fail: the header refuses the implementation directory, clause 3 preserves condition 5 as the only implementation authorization, clause 4 refuses the file 08 edit under MF-6 and defers a cell note as a separate act, file 08 measures unchanged at its cited digest, and git reports zero changes under docs/v2/architecture.
The non-interference claim is accurate: 'D-082 is ADOPTED at e6460ea3… This file does not adopt or overturn D-082', and reversibility adds 'Does not overturn D-055, D-082, D-054, or D-057.'
I wrote one file, the verdict named for me, and edited and committed nothing.

The Codex verdict on the v3 disposition. Its digest verifies at bd6a8c2f… but I did not open it, so its recital as ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES with RB-DR011-CX-A1 / A2 rests on this entry's statement. My own recital I verified absolutely, and the two defects those findings address I confirmed independently during the D-082 cycle.
Whether the V1 coordinator and each surface owner, as humans, would record this. That belongs to D-054, which this entry exercises rather than re-argues.

The merits of the v3 disposition beyond my separate ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES review of it, whose stated limits I carry forward — including that I did not audit what any residual requires to close, and did not evaluate the union of what the nine pinned dispositions collectively permit.

The sixteen residuals themselves. This entry leaves every one not CLOSED, which is the conservative disposition, but I did not re-audit their statuses this cycle beyond confirming DR-011's row still leads HARD-BLOCKED.
Whether a later file 08 cell note correctly reflects this recording. Clause 4 defers it under MF-6, the overturn clause names it, and no such edit exists.

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. The single most important thing this entry could have got wrong is losing v3's hard-won bound at the recording step — v2 of that disposition was rejected for granting an unbounded surface, and an owner recording that quietly reverted to the broad form would undo the repair while looking compliant. Clause 2 carries 'This parent adds no independent semantic permission' verbatim into the recording and the entry grants nothing of its own. All three riders are carried three times each with correct descriptions, including the A3 direction, which I checked specifically because D-010 and DR-010 both exist and an inverted correction would be invisible at a glance — a habit I adopted after missing that exact reference one cycle ago. The unnamed 'any other row' form is right here rather than weak: all nine of DR-002 through DR-010 already carry owner-recording notes and DR-001 is SATISFIED, so DR-011 is the last row and there is no sibling left to bundle.
